items.title: Bob Kinkel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 31, 2012
items.q: I’ve known Sam. We were talking. It turns out I was one of the kids that got hired to help move Sam in.

ctx.x: This is really fascinating stuff for me. What do you envision yourself doing — I mean like you came here for a month, and I’m sorry I didn’t get to know you better before this month is up. But do you do this kind of thing more — is this something that is on your radar? © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -22-

Yeah. I always thought being a college professor is like the ultimate kind of retirement job. You know, it’s got a great schedule and just being able, and I’ve always loved teaching people, whether it’s one-on-one or working with people. I’ve taken interns and just shown them how to make things work. And I’ve always come and done like one-off classes where I’ll come in and be the guest lecturer for the day. So I’ve been doing that for a long time. And the last time I did that was last year, I came up for one of…

It’s terrific that these students are getting the real deal from someone who’s done it. Because sometimes in music schools the professors are sort of twice removed from the real world. At least that’s been my observation. It’s not that they’re not good musicians, but they may not have experienced the real thing for any length of time. So I’m glad you got to do this. In fact I have, I can pick your brain on this. I have a couple of students now who, you know they wanted to go into music and they think they want to…
